Spec 04 Basic UI (Godot) — semantic diff

Branch feature/godot-mvpBase ad1fa1a (Close spec 03)Head 5585efb Target main (one pull request at the end of the run)Date 2026-11-21 Commits 11Files 84 · +4103 / −150 Written by REVIEW: + CODE REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

Spec 04 replaces the Godot game's bare start screen with a home screen built on a new UI foundation: one theme, one screen autoload, one Back button and a session GameState. Six fighters built in code with 14 skins, a fighter list, a fighter screen with skins and Select, and an info page with the 24 words were added. server/ and ui/ are unchanged.

  • All statements S1–S14 have code and tests; 104 GUT tests pass and lint is clean.
  • The game rules (catalogue, rarity, Prestige, sample progress, vocabulary) are pure and tested headless; the choice is kept in one autoload.
  • The entrance is 2.4 s, plays once per start and a click, touch or key skips it without pressing Play.
  • On a phone in portrait the shared 1280-wide stretch makes text about 9 px and Fighters/Info about 26 px tall (finding 3).
  • The skin button and the Prestige badge style themselves instead of the theme. Several new buttons are tested only by emitting pressed (findings 1, 2).

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups. Nothing is Blocking. Fix the four Should-fix findings at CLOSE; finding 3 needs a plan decision.

Spec context

2026_11_12_04_basic_ui_spec.md (#28): statements S1–S14; Steps 1–10 (all ✅); decisions D1–D12.

Semantic diff

Why: The Godot game opened on a bare start screen with Play and had no fighters, trophies, credits or shared look. Spec 04 brings the first screen that makes kids say "wow" (a big 3D fighter with an entrance, trophies, Prestige, skins), an info page for parents, and the UI foundation (one theme, one way between screens, one Back button, session state) that the later specs reuse.

Breaking: none · Checks: 7 pass · 2 n/a · 0 fail

Screens: real screenshots from a windowed Godot 4.7.2 run (a temporary capture script, removed). Before comes from a temporary worktree at ad1fa1a. 1280×720 shots are halved; 390×844 shots are full size.

Author Q&A

Why does Back on the fighter screen go home and not to the list?
D12: one rule for every Back (D2, D3); Select also goes home so the new fighter shows at once. S10 asks for home.
Is anything saved?
No. GameState starts from SampleProgress at every game start (D4, S13); the save file comes with spec 05 or 08. server/ and ui/ are unchanged.
Why are the list pictures rendered once and cached?
D7: six live sub-viewports would render six 3D scenes per frame on a phone; the pictures are rendered off-screen once per fighter and skin and kept in GameState.pictures.

39 stages[picture_key] = stage
40 if stages.is_empty():
41 return
42 var tree: SceneTree = host.get_tree()
43 for frame: int in RENDER_FRAMES:
44 await tree.process_frameawait — Suspends the function until the signal fires; here three frames so the sub-viewports have drawn.
45 for picture_key: String in stages:
46 var stage: FighterStage = stages[picture_key]
47 if not is_instance_validis_instance_valid — True while an object is not freed; the list may be left during the wait, which frees the stages.(stage):
48 continue

50 if image != null and not image.is_empty():
51 GameState.pictures[picture_key] = ImageTexture.create_from_imageImageTexture — A texture made from an Image in memory; cached in GameState.pictures for the session.(image)
52 stage.queue_free()

Good: the rules in game/ are pure and tested headless. The skip takes its event, so a tap never also presses Play. The pictures are cached, which keeps the list cheap on a phone. Premultiplied alpha is handled on both stage and card. Nothing in server/, ui/ or LICENSES.md changed. There is no debug output and no TODO. The Steps' Notes describe what was built, including deviations such as viewed_fighter.

  • The .tscn layouts besides the card and the arena: these are container trees, checked by test_screen_sizes.gd and the screenshots.
  • The spec file and .specs/features/README.md: process documents.
  • tools/export_web.ps1 and check_tools.ps1 were not re-run (Step 10 ran them; no .ps1 changed). The device play-test stays with the author (Deferred Items).

Concepts glossary

Autoload
A script registered in project.godot that Godot adds under the root once per game start. GameState is one, so its _ready resets once and the choice survives every change_scene_to_file but not a reload (S13).
Dictionary.duplicate
Returns a shallow copy. Used so the session can change trophies without changing the SampleProgress constants.
Typed loop variable
A for loop with a static type on its variable (GDScript 4.2+), as the guideline's 'static types everywhere' asks.
Guard clause
Returns early with false before anything changes, so a locked fighter or unknown skin never becomes the home fighter (S5).
Screen constant
A path constant per screen; a later spec adds one line, and tests check each constant names a real scene.
Error return
Godot's error enum (OK = 0). Returned so a caller or test can see a bad path; the screens ignore it.
SceneTree.change_scene_to_file
Frees the current scene and loads another at the end of the frame; returns an Error. Wrapped here so every screen path lives in one place (D2).
@warning_ignore
An annotation that silences one GDScript warning for the next statement; here the intended integer division.
Static function
Called on the class (Prestige.level) without an instance; the guideline's shape for pure rules in game/.
maxi
Integer maximum (global function). Clamps negative trophies to 0 so the level is never negative.
Once-per-start flag
A GameState field set when the entrance starts; returning home finds it true and skips the entrance (S2).
_input
Called for every input event before the GUI gets it; lets the home screen see a tap before a button does.
Viewport.set_input_as_handled
Marks the event as used so no Control receives it; the tap that skips does not also press Play.
Tween
A lightweight animation object bound to the node; it interpolates properties over time and is freed when finished or killed.
Tween.set_parallel
Makes the following tweeners run at the same time; each uses set_delay to start on the timeline.
Transition and ease
Choose the curve (QUAD, ELASTIC, BACK…) and its direction; used for the fall, the bounce and the title pop.
await
Suspends the function until the signal fires; here three frames so the sub-viewports have drawn.
is_instance_valid
True while an object is not freed; the list may be left during the wait, which frees the stages.
ViewportTexture.get_image
Copies the rendered pixels back from the GPU into an Image; slow, so done once per fighter and skin.
ImageTexture
A texture made from an Image in memory; cached in GameState.pictures for the session.
Theme override
Sets one theme item on one Control only; here the rarity colour from Rarity, which D1 allows.
ButtonGroup
Makes toggle buttons exclusive: pressing one releases the others; one chosen skin at a time.
Callable.bind
Adds fixed arguments to a callable; each skin button calls _on_skin_pressed with its own skin id.
Font size override
Sets the font size of one Control; D1 says screens set no font sizes except the title's.
StyleBox override
Replaces a StyleBox of the theme on this Control only; colours and borders live in the script, not in hack_star_theme.tres.
StyleBoxFlat
A box drawn from colours, borders and corner radii, without a texture.
Overlay button
A Button as the last child of a PanelContainer covers the whole card; pressing it emits opened, while a drag still scrolls the list.
StyleBoxEmpty
A StyleBox that draws nothing; the button is invisible but still takes clicks and touches.
GUT assert
A GUT 9.7.1 assertion; failing ones are listed by tools/test.ps1.
Signal.emit
Calls every connected handler directly, skipping the button's input handling and its disabled state.
Project theme
The default theme for every Control in the project; screens of later specs get the look without any work (D1).
Scene instance
A node that is a copy of another scene (back_button.tscn); changes to that scene reach every screen.
